newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Fortis AG to raise capital by 17 billion Bfr.
newsitem.headline: Fortis AG to raise capital by 17 billion Bfr.

text.p: Fortis AG, the Belgian arm of Belgian-Dutch insurance group Fortis, said on Wednesday it planned to raise 17 billion Belgian francs to pay for recent acquisitions by issuing new shares.

In a statement, Fortis AG said one issue would be reserved for shareholders, the other for staff. Subscriptions for shareholders will run from February 12 to 26. The number of shares allowing for subscription to new shares and their price will be based on Fortis AG's average share price on the Brussels bourse, less between eight and 12 percent, the company said. The issue will be priced by February 11.
The new shares issued will qualify for dividends from January 1, 1996. The issue will be led by ASLK-CGER Bank, Generale Bank and SBC Warburg.
"The stable shareholders of Fortis AG have expressed their intention to participate in this capital increase," the company said. Fortis AG's largest shareholder is Ste Generale de Belgique.
Fortis AG said staff would later be issued with a maximum of 80,000 new shares under the same conditions as used in the public offering.
Fortis AG said that, in view of the rights issue, it would not be proposing an optional stock dividend to shareholders in 1997, as it has done in previous years.
"As a consequence, the dividend the board of directors will submit to the approval of the general meeting of shareholders on May 28, 1997 will be entirely paid in cash," Fortis said.
Fortis AG said on Wednesday it was in talks with Belgium's privatization committee about increasing its 49.9 percent controlling interest in Belgian state-owned bank and insurance group ASLK-CGER.
Last month, Fortis, which is co-owned by Dutch insurance group Fortis AMEV, also completed a 2.5 billion guilder (46 billion franc) acquisition of Dutch investment bank MeesPierson.
Fortis AG and Fortis AMEV said they would split the cost of the acquisition. Fortis AG said at the time it was considering a rights issue.
